title: Fundamentals of Electronics
description: A practical introduction to circuits, measurement, resistors, LEDs, and safe low-voltage prototyping.
outcomes: Calculate resistance, current and power with the correct units.
Build and explain a resistor-limited LED circuit.
Measure a circuit and diagnose an open connection.
prerequisites: No prior electronics experience. Basic arithmetic and a willingness to record measurements are enough.

title: Arduino: Your First Projects
description: Program inputs and outputs, handle buttons, and build a nonblocking reaction timer with an Arduino UNO R3.
outcomes: Upload and explain a sketch for an UNO R3.
Read a button reliably and control an LED.
Build a reaction timer with a clear state model.
prerequisites: Complete EL-101 or demonstrate breadboard use, LED polarity and resistor selection.

title: Sensors & Measurement with ESP32
description: Connect sensors, interpret ADC readings, calibrate measurements, and build a documented plant-monitor prototype.
outcomes: Check voltage compatibility before connecting a sensor.
Calibrate a sensor using recorded reference points.
Separate real measurements from missing or invalid data.
prerequisites: Breadboard competence and basic embedded programming. Complete EL-102 or equivalent.

title: Robotics & Motor Control
description: Select motor drivers, measure distance safely, and implement a tested obstacle-avoiding rover state machine.
outcomes: Match a driver to the motor’s supply and current requirements.
Explain PWM control and safe direction changes.
Test a rover’s stop and sensor-failure behavior.
prerequisites: Complete EL-102 and have experience measuring low-voltage circuits. A supervisor must review moving hardware.

title: Connected IoT Systems
description: Design telemetry contracts, secure a local MQTT workflow, and test disconnected-device behavior.
outcomes: Define and validate a device telemetry message.
Use authenticated MQTT with clear topic permissions.
Test reconnects, stale readings and duplicate messages.
prerequisites: Complete EL-201. Familiarity with JSON, IP networking and embedded code is required.

title: Embedded Design & Reliability
description: Turn a breadboard prototype into an engineered system with power budgeting, timing analysis and repeatable verification.
outcomes: Build a power and timing budget from documented requirements.
Define startup, watchdog and fault recovery behavior.
Create a repeatable verification and handover package.
prerequisites: Complete EL-202 and EL-301 or demonstrate comparable embedded-system experience.

title: AI Essentials
description: Understand AI capabilities and limits, assess everyday tasks, and verify a useful AI-assisted work product.
outcomes: Distinguish rule-based automation, machine learning and generative AI.
Choose a suitable task and define a useful result.
Check factual claims and protect sensitive information.
prerequisites: No coding experience. Familiarity with documents, spreadsheets and a web browser is enough.

title: Prompting & Practical AI
description: Create repeatable prompts for summarization, extraction and drafting, with review rubrics and evidence checks.
outcomes: Build a reusable prompt with explicit boundaries.
Extract structured data and validate the result.
Compare prompt versions with a fixed evaluation set.
prerequisites: Complete AI-101 or demonstrate factual verification and safe handling of workshop inputs.

title: Workflow Automation with AI
description: Build a reviewed support-request workflow in n8n with schema validation, retries and duplicate protection.
outcomes: Define a trigger, data contract and review queue.
Handle missing fields, duplicate events and service failures.
Measure workflow quality beyond successful execution.
prerequisites: Complete AI-102. Basic JSON and web-request knowledge. No advanced programming is required.

title: Grounded AI Assistants
description: Build a small document-grounded assistant with source citations, permission filtering and answerability tests.
outcomes: Explain retrieval-augmented generation and its limits.
Prepare a document collection with traceable chunks.
Evaluate answers for support, permissions and abstention.
prerequisites: Complete AI-102. Familiarity with documents and basic structured data. Programming is optional for the paper prototype.

title: Agent Workflows & Evaluation
description: Design bounded tool-using workflows and evaluate decision quality, approvals, failure handling and resource limits.
outcomes: Design tool contracts and enforce authorization outside the model.
Build repeatable evaluations with meaningful failure cases.
Compare a bounded agent against a deterministic baseline.
prerequisites: Complete AI-201 and AI-202. Comfortable with JSON, tool APIs and basic scripting or equivalent workflow logic.

title: Production AI & Automation Operations
description: Plan an AI service rollout with operational measures, cost budgets, privacy controls, incident response and rollback.
outcomes: Define quality and operational release criteria.
Estimate cost with retries and review effort included.
Exercise rollback and incident response with synthetic failures.
prerequisites: Complete AI-301 or demonstrate evaluation, controlled tool use and workflow error handling.
